open_points.subject: A13/A15 non-executed node records (`skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed`)
open_points.text: "The next node is the ready node with the smallest `node_id`..." together with "...makes its node `skipped_by_guard` without executing" and "...concludes `upstream_failed` without executing"
open_points.question: When several nodes become conclusively non-executable at once, in what exact order are their NodeExecution records written (and therefore their `attempt_number`s assigned)?
options: Emit such records immediately when each condition becomes true, in `node_id` order.
Emit them only when no ready node remains, then in `node_id` order.
Emit them lazily when first inspected/needed.
open_points.default_guess: Emit immediately once determinable, ordered by `node_id` (and `map_index` for mapped elements).

open_points.subject: Run advancement persistence boundaries around effect sending
open_points.text: "A change is one call in one transaction inside the store module" plus "Approving sends the effect at once... and marks the approval `used` when the request is sent" plus "for an operation other than `read`, its EffectAttempt is written `in_flight` durably; then the request is made and its outcome written..."
open_points.question: Which exact state updates must be committed together vs separately during approve/send/outcome so crash points are deterministic and identical across implementations?
options: Use separate commits at each durable milestone (`approval decision`, `in_flight`, `NodeExecution/outcome`, run status).
Wrap all updates for one send attempt in one transaction except the network call boundary.
Use one transaction for the whole request handler advancement loop.
open_points.default_guess: Commit at each explicit durable milestone, with `in_flight` committed before network send and outcome committed after response classification.

open_points.subject: A16 config re-read failure scope
open_points.text: "A changed configuration that fails a check of the start makes every request refused... until a valid one is read; ... Only the token list is taken from a re-read; every other field ... only at a restart."
open_points.question: On hot re-read, which start checks are re-applied to decide 'every request refused' if only token fields are intended to be reloaded?
options: Re-validate only token-list-related checks (format, uniqueness, length).
Re-validate full startup config checks even for fields not hot-reloaded.
Refuse only requests whose auth decision depends on invalid re-read content.
open_points.default_guess: Re-validate only token-list-related checks on hot re-read; keep full-config checks as startup-only.
